title: surge-sentinel-eviction-and-fast-fallback-for-regional-surge
author: Ava Sinclair
description:
Motivation: During the last regional traffic spike we observed a fast-moving token surge that caused SLO breaches despite existing circuit breakers and soft-degradation policies. This PR introduces a lightweight "surge sentinel" that detects atypical per-region token velocity and preemptively evicts low-priority, non-interactive requests while enabling an automatic fast-fallback to smaller, quantized model variants for interactive routes. The goal is to reduce tail latency and prevent full regional circuit trips while preserving high-priority throughput and preserving cache locality where possible.

What this PR does (summary):
- Adds a Surge Sentinel component to the regional router that computes a rolling token-velocity score and triggers an eviction window when thresholds are exceeded.
- Implements prioritized eviction rules: requests are bucketed by priority (api-key tier + route importance) and eviction targets low-priority buckets first.
- Fast-fallback policy: for interactive (chat/generation) routes, seamlessly route to a pinned quantized variant (q4) with KV-cache migration when capacity for full model is constrained.
- Circuit state persistence: when a region demotes traffic, the sentinel persists ephemeral circuit metadata to the regional metadata store so downstream routers can apply consistent backoff without flapping.
- Safe-drain KV cache: improves the KV cache drain path for model switchovers so prefix caches for promoted fallback models are warmed via async copy instead of blocking the request path.
- Metrics + tracing: adds surge_sentinal.trigger, surge_evicted.count, surge_fallbacks.count and tracing tags (surge.score, surge.window_ms) and a small dashboard tile.
- Runbook & automated rollback: adds an emergency runbook section and a feature flag to disable sentinel per-region.

Design notes:
- The sentinel uses a short window (default 15s) with exponential backoff for repeated triggers to avoid oscillations. Thresholds are configured per-customer tier so enterprise customers can opt-out via policy.
- Eviction is best-effort: we do not drop in-flight high-priority requests and we prefer fallback routing over hard failures where possible.
- KV cache migration is asynchronous and bounded (configurable max-copy-per-second) to avoid amplifying load during surges.

Checklist (author):
- [x] Unit tests for surge scoring and priority selection
- [x] Integration test simulating regional token surge and verifying fallback routing
- [x] Added metrics and tracing hooks
- [x] Runbook excerpt and feature flag documented
- [x] Smoke-tested in perf-canary with synthetic surge profile

Commits (high level):
- 8f3c9d2 - core: add regional surge sentinel and token velocity monitor
- a2b1f5e - router: eviction decision logic and priority buckets
- c7d2b44 - routing: fast-fallback path and q4 model pinning
- d9a8ee1 - kvcache: non-blocking async copy and bounded migration controller
- e5f11b3 - metrics: add surge_*, tracing tags and dashboard tile
- f1c44b0 - tests: unit/integration tests for sentinel and fallback
- 02b7c9a - docs: runbook excerpt and feature flag docs

Files changed (high level):
- src/router/sentinel/surge_sentinel.go (new): main sentinel logic and configuration
- src/router/prioritizer/eviction_policy.go: priority buckets and selection algorithm adjustments
- src/router/fallback/fallback_router.go: fast-fallback path + model pinning hooks
- src/kvcache/migration_controller.go: async copy controller and rate limiter
- src/telemetry/metrics_registry.go: new metrics registration and tagging
- infra/feature_flags.yaml: per-region sentinel enable flag with default on
- docs/runbooks/surge-sentinel.md: runbook excerpt and rollback steps
- tests/integration/surge_sentinel_test.go: simulated surge scenarios
- charts/sentinel-values.yaml: helm toggles for private/dedicated installs

Review notes / discussion (high level):
- Ethan Park: "This looks good; main concern is ensuring the async KV migration doesn't create a second surge. Please add a strict per-region migration cap and unit test for throttling."
- Author (Ava): "Added bounded migration controller (rate-limiter) and unit tests (see migration_controller_test). The cap is configurable via helm and defaults to 250KB/s per node."
- Sofia Martinez: "Can the fallback path maintain deterministic latency for streaming responses? We should avoid introducing head-of-line blocking."
- Author: "Fallback path streams directly from the quantized model runtime; KV warm-up is parallel and non-blocking. Added tracing flags to detect any H-O-L events."
- Liam O'Connor: "Approve after CI green and a short canary run in eu-west1."

CI summary:
- unit: pass
- integration (canary profile): pass (perf-canary run: 10m synthetic surge, no SLO breach for high-priority lanes)
- lint: pass (minor nits fixed in follow-up commit)

Canary & rollout plan:
- Step 1: Deploy feature gate off in main and enable in perf-canary cluster for 24h (completed).
- Step 2: Monitor surge_sentinal.trigger and surge_evicted.count and SLOs for 1h, then enable for eu-west1 (rolled out).
- Step 3: Gradual roll to other regions over 6h with automated rollback if SLO regressions > 2x baseline.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged after canary validation and one post-merge smoke check in eu-west1. Will follow up with a minor tuning PR to adjust default thresholds based on canary telemetry.

Notes for ops:
- Feature flag: router.sentinel.enabled.{region} = true/false
- Emergency disable: set router.sentinel.enabled.{region} = false and restart router service; sentinel has fast-stop mode to clear windows on shutdown.
- Observability: the new dashboard tile is under Observability > Reliability > Surge Sentinel

Related: ENG-5421 (design doc), ENG-5480 (runbook), SUP-3421 (customer incident tracing).

release_notes: Add Surge Sentinel to mitigate rapid token surges: preemptive low-priority eviction, fast fallback to quantized models, safe async KV cache warming, metrics and runbook. Default behavior enabled per-region; can be disabled via feature flag.
notes: Follow-up PR planned to tune default thresholds after wider regional telemetry; ops advised to monitor surge.evicted and fallback counts during rollout.
